annotation.title_clean: ICO v Clearview AI Inc (Privacy International intervening) [2025] UKUT 319 (AAC)
annotation.title_en: ICO v Clearview AI Inc (Privacy International intervening) [2025] UKUT 319 (AAC)
annotation.summary_en: UK Upper Tribunal decision allowing the Information Commissioner's appeal against Clearview AI. It holds that Clearview's web-scraped facial recognition database processing falls within the material and territorial scope of the EU and UK GDPR (behavioural monitoring, 'related to'), so the ICO had jurisdiction. The matter is remitted to the First-tier Tribunal.
key_provisions_or_claims: Article 2(2)(a) GDPR excludes only activities where Member States reserved competence, not all matters outside Union competence.
'Behavioural monitoring' in Article 3(2)(b) is broad and includes passive automated collection and profiling; no human watchfulness needed.
'Related to' in Article 3(2) covers controllers whose processing relates to monitoring by another controller.
Clearview's processing is within the territorial scope of the UK and EU GDPR.
FTT decision set aside; remitted on the basis that the ICO had jurisdiction to issue the £7.55m penalty and enforcement notices.
